Below is a conservative, cardiac‑rehab–informed 12‑week general fitness program designed for a 58‑year‑old male, six months post–myocardial infarction, cleared for moderate intensity only. It keeps HR under ~70% of age‑predicted max (~115 bpm), avoids Valsalva and maximal lifts, emphasizes gradual progression, symptom monitoring, and full‑body conditioning. It uses RPE 3–5/10 (moderate), talk test (able to speak in full sentences), and includes longer warm‑ups/cool‑downs.

Global guardrails
- Intensity: Keep HR ≤115 bpm and RPE 3–5/10. If he’s on beta‑blockers, lean more on RPE and talk test rather than HR alone.
- Breathing: No Valsalva. Cue exhale on exertion, inhale on return. Use controlled tempo (2–3 sec up, 2–3 sec down).
- Blood pressure safety: Avoid overhead strain with breath holding and rapid position changes. Sit/stand slowly.
- Pain/ischemia check: Stop if chest pain/pressure, unusual shortness of breath, palpitations, dizziness, or radiating pain. If symptoms persist >5 minutes or don’t resolve with rest, follow emergency protocol.
- Progression: Only 5–10% weekly load volume increase (time, sets, or incline), not all at once.
- Frequency target: 5 days/week (3 mixed cardio+strength sessions, 2 lighter cardio+mobility days), 2 rest days.
- Hydration/temperature: Avoid very hot environments; encourage hydration.
- Blood glucose if applicable: If on diabetes meds, monitor pre/post as advised by care team.

Program structure overview
- Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Reintroduction and base building. Emphasis on steady cardio, fundamental movement patterns, light resistance, longer warm‑ups/cool‑downs.
- Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Progressive overload within moderate intensity. Slightly longer sessions, introduce gentle intervals, add single‑leg stability, cable work.
- Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Consolidation and functional capacity. Maintain moderate zones, modest density increases, light circuits, balance/rotational control.

Weekly schedule template

Strength training parameters
- Intensity: ~40–60% estimated 1RM or a load you can lift 12–15 reps with 2–3 reps in reserve. No max testing.
- Tempo: 2–0–2 or 3–0–3; steady breathing.
- Rest: 60–90 seconds between sets; extend if HR creeps up.
- Machines/cables/free weights permitted; prioritize machines for safety as needed.
- Stop sets if technique degrades or if HR exceeds target.

Cardio parameters
- Steady state at RPE 3–5; HR ≤115 bpm.
- Gentle intervals introduced only in Phase 2–3 as 1–2 min slightly higher RPE 4–5 followed by longer easy periods, without exceeding HR cap.

- Day 3 (Mixed B)

Week 4

Goals: Slight volume increase and introduce controlled intervals; introduce unilateral stability. Session length 55–65 minutes.

Week 5

Goals: Maintain moderate intensity while slightly improving density and functional movements. Introduce simple circuits to keep HR steady in target zone. Session length 60–70 minutes as tolerated.

Week 11

  - Swap seated row for chest‑supported dumbbell row.
  - Swap leg press for hack squat machine with shallow range if comfortable, otherwise keep leg press.

Week 12
- Cardio: 15 min steady + 3 x 2–3 min RPE 4–5 with 3 min easy; light days 45–50 min steady.
- Strength: Deload density slightly to finish feeling strong: 2 rounds per circuit, keep reps 10–12, perfect form and breathing. Finish with extended cool‑down and breathing.

Mobility and core (can be sprinkled in warm‑ups/cool‑downs)
- Daily 5–10 minutes: Thoracic openers, pec doorway stretch, hip flexor stretch, hamstring stretch, calf stretch.

Monitoring and progression notes
- Keep a simple log: RPE, peak HR, symptoms, BP pre/post if recommended by his clinician.
- Progress only one variable per week: time, reps, or a small load increase (1–2 kg), not all.
- If any session exceeds HR cap or RPE >5, reduce next session volume by ~10–15%.

Nutrition and recovery (general, non‑prescriptive)
- Heart‑healthy pattern: Emphasize vegetables, fruits, legumes, whole grains, nuts, seeds, fish 2x/week, lean poultry; prioritize olive oil; limit sodium, added sugars, and processed meats; align with any clinician or dietitian guidance.
- Protein: ~1.0–1.2 g/kg/day unless contraindicated; distribute across meals to support recovery.
- Hydration: 1.5–2.5 L/day adjusted for meds and climate; avoid large fluid boluses if on fluid restriction.
- Pre‑exercise: Light snack 60–90 min before if needed (fruit + yogurt, small oatmeal).

Contraindications and red flags recap
- Stop exercise and seek medical help if chest pain, severe shortness of breath, dizziness/syncope, palpitations, new leg swelling, or unusual fatigue occurs.
- No breath holding; avoid heavy overhead lifts, forced reps, or high‑intensity intervals.
- Maintain good foot support; avoid straining during bowel movements around workouts.

Equipment substitutions
- If knee discomfort: Replace step‑ups with leg press or TRX assisted squat.
- If shoulder discomfort: Replace chest press with cable press at lower angle or floor press with very light DBs.
- If back discomfort: Replace RDLs with hip hinge using dowel or bridge variations.

Here’s a practical, cardiac‑health–focused nutrition plan to pair with the 12‑week program. Global principles
- Pattern: Largely Mediterranean/DASH
  - Vegetables and fruits: ≥5 servings/day (aim for 2 fruit + 3+ veg; include leafy greens, berries, crucifers).
  - Whole grains: Oats, barley, brown/wild rice, quinoa, whole‑grain bread/pasta.
  - Legumes: Beans, lentils, chickpeas 4–7x/week (fiber and plant protein).
  - Healthy fats: Extra‑virgin olive oil as primary added fat; nuts/seeds daily (almonds, walnuts, pistachios, chia, flax).
  - Lean proteins: Fish (especially fatty fish) 2–3x/week; skinless poultry; low‑fat dairy or fortified alternatives; plant proteins.
  - Limit: Processed meats, refined carbs/sweets, deep‑fried foods, high‑sodium packaged items, excess alcohol.
- Sodium: Target 1,500–2,000 mg/day unless clinician sets otherwise. Prioritize fresh foods; rinse canned beans/veg; choose “no salt added.”
- Fiber: 30–40 g/day (gradually). Supports LDL reduction, satiety, and glycemic control.
- Added sugars: ≤6–9 tsp (24–36 g)/day; favor whole fruit over juice.
- Fats: Emphasize mono- and polyunsaturated; keep saturated fat <7–10% of calories; avoid trans fats.
- Omega‑3s: Aim for 2–3 servings/week of salmon, sardines, trout, or mackerel; if not met, discuss EPA/DHA supplement with clinician (especially if on anticoagulants or with bleeding risk).
- Alcohol: If used, keep ≤1 drink/day, with food, and only if approved by care team; none is also fine.
- Hydration: Generally 1.5–2.5 L/day unless fluid‑restricted; spread through day. Extra 300–500 mL across workouts, not chugged at once.

Energy and protein targets
- Weight maintenance or gradual loss (if needed): Create a modest 250–400 kcal/day deficit. Avoid aggressive dieting.
- Protein: ~1.0–1.2 g/kg/day distributed across 3–4 meals (e.g., 25–35 g/meal) to support recovery without undue renal load (confirm if CKD).
- Carbs: Center on high‑fiber, low‑GI sources; time most carbs around breakfast/lunch or post‑exercise.
- Micronutrients of focus: Potassium, magnesium, calcium (from plants/dairy), and nitrates (beets, arugula) for BP; plant sterols (fortified foods), soluble fiber (oats, barley, psyllium) for LDL.

- Weeks 9–12 (Consolidation): Personalize portions, add cardioprotective extras, lock habits.

  - Chest-supported row 4 x 8–10
  - Step-up 3 x 8–10/side
  - Hamstring curl 3 x 10–12
- Day 2 Strength B + easy cardio
  - Trap-bar deadlift from blocks (lower blocks only if prior weeks symptom-free) 3–4 x 5–6
  - Machine chest press or cable press 4 x 8–10
  - Pallof press 3 x 10–12/side
  - Dead bug 3 x 10/side
  - Cardio: 10–12 min easy
- Day 3 Rest/easy walk
- Day 4 Strength C
  - Goblet or double-DB front squat 4 x 6–8 (stop 2–3 reps in reserve)
  - Lat pulldown 3 x 8–10
  - 1-arm DB row 3–4 x 8–10/side
  - Calf raise 3 x 12–15
- Day 5 Strength D + easy cardio
  - DB RDL 3–4 x 8–10 (or maintain trap-bar if preferred; choose one hinge per day)
  - Cable fly or press 3 x 10–12
  - Face pull 3 x 12–15
  - External rotation 2–3 x 12–15
  - Farmer carry 3 x 30–40 m
  - Cardio: 10–12 min easy
- Cardio: 260–280 min/week. Intervals: 8–10 x 90 sec RPE 4–5 with 2 min easy; Two steady 45–55 min sessions.

Week 10
- Strength: Micro-load (+1–2 kg) the first lift each day if RPE ≤4, HR ≤115, technique pristine. Keep sets the same.
- Cardio: Maintain 260–280 min/week or add 10–15 min total if recovery excellent. One intervals session (5 x 3 min RPE 4–5, 3 min easy), two steady 50–55 min sessions.

Week 11
- Strength: Optionally add one extra accessory set to upper and lower (e.g., +1 set face pulls; +1 set ham curls) if recovery strong. Keep big lifts at 3–4 x 6–8.
- Cardio: 270–290 min/week. Intervals similar to Week 10; one 55–60 min steady session; one 45–50 min steady session.

Week 12 (Deload strength, maintain cardio or slight taper if fatigued)
- Strength: Reduce volume ~30% (drop one set per exercise). Keep loads; focus on perfect reps and breathing.
- Cardio: 260–300 min depending on fatigue; keep everything moderate. If planning any fitness assessment (submax), schedule it 3–4 days after last harder cardio.

Technique and coaching cues for squats/deadlifts
- Squat: Feet shoulder-width; sit to box early on; knees track over toes; keep chest tall. Exhale as you stand.
- Trap-bar block pull: Neutral spine; shoulders down/back; push through mid-foot; reset, breathe between reps; no touch-and-go.
- RDL: Hips back, soft knees, neutral spine; go to just below knees; exhale as you rise.
- Use safeties/spotter for squats; stop a set if breath wants to “hold.”

Cardiac-safe performance testing and events
- Unless a clinician upgrades clearance beyond moderate intensity, avoid a true 5K time trial. Instead, use:
  - 6-Minute Walk Test (distance, HR, RPE).
  - Modified Rockport 1-Mile Walk (stay under HR cap).
  - Brisk 5K walk “completion” within HR limits as a celebratory event.
- If the cardiologist later approves higher intensity, you can integrate a cautious run-walk progression and a capped-effort 5K per their HR/BP limits.

Nutrition plan (cardiac-health focused, supports fat loss and recovery)
- Pattern: Mediterranean/DASH.
  - Vegetables/fruits ≥5 servings/day; legumes 4–7x/week; whole grains; nuts/seeds daily; fish (especially fatty) 2–3x/week; EVOO as primary fat.
  - Limit processed meats, refined sugars, fried/high-sodium foods, alcohol (≤1 drink/day if approved).
- Sodium: 1,500–2,000 mg/day unless clinician specifies otherwise.
- Fiber: 30–40 g/day (gradual increase).
- Fats: Emphasize mono-/polyunsaturated; saturated fat <7–10% kcal; avoid trans fats.
- Protein: ~1.1–1.2 g/kg/day, 25–35 g/meal, leucine-rich sources (dairy, eggs, soy, fish, poultry). Supports anti-sarcopenia strength goals.
- Carbs: High-fiber, lower-GI; time more carbs around breakfast/lunch or post-exercise.
- Omega-3s: Fish 2–3x/week; consider EPA/DHA only with clinician approval.
- Energy for weight loss: Aim for 0.3–0.7% body weight loss/week via ~300–500 kcal/day deficit (diet first, cardio supports).
- Hydration: 1.5–2.5 L/day unless fluid-restricted; spread fluids; modest extra around workouts.

12-week nutrition rollout highlights
- Weeks 1–2: Switch to EVOO, log sodium, hit ≥5 veg/fruit servings/day, swap to whole grains, start 2 fish meals.
- Weeks 3–4: Legumes ≥3x/week, add 1 Tbsp ground flax/chia daily, keep added sugars <30 g/day.
- Weeks 5–6: Fiber 30–35 g/day; nuts/seeds daily; beets/arugula 3x/week for nitrates; minimize butter fully.
- Weeks 7–8: 4+ legume meals/week; 2–3 fish meals/week consistently; consider plant sterol–fortified foods if LDL high (ask clinician).
- Weeks 9–10: Portion tune to stay in deficit; ensure protein 25–35 g each meal; fermented food daily if sodium allows.
- Weeks 11–12: Reduce restaurant meals to ≤1–2/week; build a 2-week rotating menu and a grocery list of 10 go-to meals.

Sample daily template
- Breakfast: Oats with berries, walnuts, chia/flax; or veggie omelet + whole-grain toast; or Greek yogurt parfait.
- Lunch: Lentil/bean soup + salad; quinoa bowl with chickpeas/veg/EVOO; or whole-grain wrap (grilled chicken/tempeh + hummus + veg).
- Dinner: Salmon + farro + broccoli; chicken + sweet potato + greens; or bean chili over brown rice + salad.
- Snacks: Fruit + nuts; carrots + hummus; plain yogurt with berries; cottage cheese + pineapple; edamame; popcorn (unsalted).

Recovery and adjuncts
- Sleep: 7–8 hours, consistent schedule.
- Creatine monohydrate: Discuss with cardiologist; if approved and renal function normal, 3 g/day (no loading) may aid strength.
- Avoid NSAIDs for soreness unless advised; use mobility, light walking, or 10–15 min easy cycling to reduce DOMS.

Substitutions for joint comfort
- Knees: Use leg press or hack squat (shallow) instead of squats; low box step-ups/TRX-assisted squat.
- Low back/hips: Glute bridge/hip thrust or cable pull-through instead of deadlifts.
- Shoulders/wrists: Smith box squat or safety-bar squat; swap cable press angles as needed.

Monitoring
- Keep a simple log: exercises, sets/reps, loads, peak HR, RPE, symptoms. Record cardio minutes and steps.
- If HR or RPE regularly exceed targets, reduce next session volume by 10–20% or add rest day.
- Coordinate with his cardiologist/dietitian for medication–nutrition interactions and any update to exercise clearance (especially before any performance testing or intensity changes).

This integrated plan builds practical strength with safe compound patterns, meaningfully increases weekly cardio for weight loss within moderate limits, and aligns nutrition to cardiac health and recovery over the full 12 weeks.

Below is the complete 12-week program integrating all adjustments: cardiac-safe guardrails, expanded strength emphasis (4 strength days/week), compound lift variants (squats/deadlifts), upgraded but still moderate-only cardio progression for weight loss, and the cardiac-focused nutrition plan. It’s written for a 58-year-old male, 6 months post-MI, cleared for moderate intensity only (HR ≤ ~115 bpm, ~70% APMHR). No Valsalva, no max lifts, RPE 3–5/10. If on beta-blockers, use RPE and talk test primarily.

Global safety guardrails (apply every session)
- HR cap: ≤115 bpm (or clinician’s prescription). RPE ≤5/10; talk test = full sentences.
- Breathing: Exhale on exertion every rep; inhale on return. No breath holding.
- Progression: Change only one variable at a time (time, reps, load, or incline). 5–10% weekly volume/time increase max.
- Rest: 90–120 s for big lifts, 60–90 s for accessories; add 30–60 s if HR trends up.
- Stop/modify if chest pain/pressure, unusual dyspnea, dizziness, palpitations, or radiating pain. If symptoms persist, follow emergency protocol.
- Warm-up 10–12 min (gradual cardio ramp + dynamic mobility); cool-down 8–10 min (easy cardio + breathing 3–4 s inhale, 4–6 s exhale + gentle stretching).

Weekly schedule template (Phase 1–3)
- Day 1: Strength A (Squat focus + Back + Core)
- Day 2: Strength B (Hinge focus + Push + Core) + 10–15 min easy cardio
- Day 3: Rest or 20–30 min easy walk (RPE 2–3)
- Day 4: Strength C (Squat variation + Pull + Calves)
- Day 5: Strength D (Hinge variation + Push balance + Carries) + 10–15 min easy cardio
- Day 6: Dedicated Cardio (moderate) + Mobility
- Day 7: Cardio (moderate) or Rest depending on fatigue
- Daily steps target: Progress toward 8–10k/day by Weeks 10–12.

Strength training parameters (across all weeks)
- Loads: Start ~45–60% estimated 1RM; progress toward 55–65% if HR/RPE remain within limits. Keep 2–3 reps in reserve.
- Reps: Big lifts mostly 6–10 reps (never grinding); accessories 10–15.
- Tempo: 2–3 sec down, brief pause, 2–3 sec up. Reset between deadlift reps.
- Squat/deadlift variants: Goblet/Smith box squats; trap-bar deadlift from blocks or RDLs. No barbell back squats or floor deadlifts initially.

Cardio parameters (fat loss focus, still moderate)
- Warm up and cool down every time; stay RPE 3–5; HR ≤115 bpm.
- Modality: Treadmill walking with incline, bike (upright/recumbent), elliptical low ramp. Rotate to reduce joint stress.
- Weekly time goals: Build from ~180–200 min/week (Weeks 1–2) to 260–300 min/week by Weeks 9–12 if recovery allows.

PHASE 1 — Foundation and movement quality (Weeks 1–4)
Goals: Groove squat/hinge patterns, expand total weekly strength sets, establish moderate cardio frequency and technique.

Week 1
- Day 1 Strength A
  - Goblet box squat (to knee-height) 3 x 10–12
  - Seated row (neutral) 3 x 10–12
  - Step-up low box (support) 2 x 10/side
  - Hamstring curl (machine) 2 x 12–15
  - Pallof press 2 x 10–12/side
- Day 2 Strength B + easy cardio
  - DB/Kettlebell RDL 3 x 10–12
  - Chest press (machine) 3 x 10–12
  - Incline push-up (elevated) 2 x 8–12
  - Cable face pull 2 x 12–15
  - Dead bug 2 x 8–10/side
  - Cardio: 10–12 min easy (RPE 3–4)
- Day 3 Rest or 20–30 min easy walk
- Day 4 Strength C
  - Goblet box squat 3 x 8–10
  - 1-arm DB supported row 3 x 10–12/side
  - Lat pulldown 2 x 10–12
  - Seated calf raise 2 x 12–15
  - Single-leg balance (fingertip support) 2 x 20–30s/side
- Day 5 Strength D + easy cardio
  - Hip hinge drill with dowel 1–2 sets
  - DB RDL (light) 3 x 10–12
  - Cable chest fly or press 2 x 10–12
  - External rotation 2 x 12–15
  - Farmer carry light 2 x 20–30 m
  - Cardio: 10–12 min easy
- Day 6 Cardio steady: 30–35 min RPE 3–4
- Day 7 Cardio steady (optional) 25–30 min RPE 3 or Rest

Week 2
- Strength: Add 1 set to first two lifts on each strength day (priority moves). Keep reps similar.
- Cardio: 180–200 total minutes. One steady 35–40 min session + one 30–35 min; add 6 x 1 min moderate upticks with 2 min easy in one session (HR ≤115).

Week 3
- Strength:
  - Goblet box squat 4 x 8–10 (option: box 1–2 cm lower if perfect)
  - DB RDL 4 x 8–10
  - Add carries to Day 1 and 5: 2–3 x 30–40 m
- Cardio: 200–220 min/week. Intervals: 8 x 1 min RPE 4–5 with 2 min easy (stay under HR cap). Two steady 35–40 min sessions.

Week 4
- Strength: Maintain sets; nudge loads +1–2 kg if RPE ≤4, HR stable. Keep accessories 2–3 x 12–15.
- Cardio: Mixed days keep 10–15 min easy. Dedicated cardio 35–45 min steady. Optional recovery walk 20–30 min another day.

  - Incline push-up 3 x 8–12
  - Pallof press 3 x 10–12/side
  - Cardio: 10–12 min easy

  - 1-arm DB supported row 3–4 x 8–10/side

  - Seated calf raise 3 x 12–15

  - External rotation 2–3 x 12–15
  - Farmer carry 2–3 x 30–40 m
  - Cardio: 10–12 min easy

- Day 7 Cardio steady: 40–45 min RPE 3–4

Week 6
- Strength: Keep sets; add small load where RPE ≤4 and HR stable. Optional: Smith box squat replaces one goblet session if form/BP better supported.
- Cardio: 220–240 min/week. Intervals session: 6–8 x 1 min; two steady 40–45 min sessions; 1 optional 20–30 min easy walk.

Week 7
- Day 1 Strength A
  - Smith box squat or goblet squat 4 x 8
  - Chest-supported row 4 x 8–10
  - Step-downs small range 2 x 8–10/side
  - Hamstring curl 3 x 10–12

  - Trap-bar deadlift from blocks 3–4 x 6–8
  - Chest press 4 x 8–10
  - Incline push-up 3 x 8–12
  - Pallof press 3 x 10–12/side
  - Cardio: 10–12 min easy
- Day 3 Rest/easy walk
- Day 4 Strength C
  - Goblet squat to box 3–4 x 8–10
  - Lat pulldown 3 x 8–10

PHASE 3 — Consolidation and higher weekly minutes (Weeks 9–12)
Goals: Sustain weekly strength volume, polish technique, slightly increase cardio minutes for weight loss while staying moderate.

  - Dead bug 3 x 10/side
  - Cardio: 10–12 min easy

- Strength: Micro-load (+1–2 kg) the first lift each day if RPE ≤4, HR ≤115, technique pristine. Keep sets the same.

Week 11

Week 12 (Deload strength, maintain cardio or slight taper if fatigued)
- Strength: Reduce volume ~30% (drop one set per exercise). Keep loads; focus on perfect reps and breathing.
- Cardio: 260–300 min depending on fatigue; keep everything moderate. If planning any fitness assessment (submax), schedule it 3–4 days after last harder cardio.

Technique and coaching cues for squats/deadlifts
- Squat: Feet shoulder-width; sit to box early on; knees track over toes; keep chest tall. Exhale as you stand.
- Trap-bar block pull: Neutral spine; shoulders down/back; push through mid-foot; reset, breathe between reps; no touch-and-go.
- RDL: Hips back, soft knees, neutral spine; go to just below knees; exhale as you rise.
- Use safeties/spotter for squats; stop a set if breath wants to “hold.”

Cardiac-safe performance testing and events
- Unless a clinician upgrades clearance beyond moderate intensity, avoid a true 5K time trial. Instead, use:
  - 6-Minute Walk Test (distance, HR, RPE).
  - Modified Rockport 1-Mile Walk (stay under HR cap).
  - Brisk 5K walk “completion” within HR limits as a celebratory event.
- If the cardiologist later approves higher intensity, you can integrate a cautious run-walk progression and a capped-effort 5K per their HR/BP limits.

Nutrition plan (cardiac-health focused, supports fat loss and recovery)
- Pattern: Mediterranean/DASH.
  - Vegetables/fruits ≥5 servings/day; legumes 4–7x/week; whole grains; nuts/seeds daily; fish (especially fatty) 2–3x/week; EVOO as primary fat.
  - Limit processed meats, refined sugars, fried/high-sodium foods, alcohol (≤1 drink/day if approved).
- Sodium: 1,500–2,000 mg/day unless clinician specifies otherwise.
- Fiber: 30–40 g/day (gradual increase).
- Fats: Emphasize mono-/polyunsaturated; saturated fat <7–10% kcal; avoid trans fats.
- Protein: ~1.1–1.2 g/kg/day, 25–35 g/meal, leucine-rich sources (dairy, eggs, soy, fish, poultry). Supports anti-sarcopenia strength goals.
- Carbs: High-fiber, lower-GI; time more carbs around breakfast/lunch or post-exercise.
- Omega-3s: Fish 2–3x/week; consider EPA/DHA only with clinician approval.
- Energy for weight loss: Aim for 0.3–0.7% body weight loss/week via ~300–500 kcal/day deficit (diet first, cardio supports).
- Hydration: 1.5–2.5 L/day unless fluid-restricted; spread fluids; modest extra around workouts.

12-week nutrition rollout highlights
- Weeks 1–2: Switch to EVOO, log sodium, hit ≥5 veg/fruit servings/day, swap to whole grains, start 2 fish meals.
- Weeks 3–4: Legumes ≥3x/week, add 1 Tbsp ground flax/chia daily, keep added sugars <30 g/day.
- Weeks 5–6: Fiber 30–35 g/day; nuts/seeds daily; beets/arugula 3x/week for nitrates; minimize butter fully.
- Weeks 7–8: 4+ legume meals/week; 2–3 fish meals/week consistently; consider plant sterol–fortified foods if LDL high (ask clinician).
- Weeks 9–10: Portion tune to stay in deficit; ensure protein 25–35 g each meal; fermented food daily if sodium allows.
- Weeks 11–12: Reduce restaurant meals to ≤1–2/week; build a 2-week rotating menu and a grocery list of 10 go-to meals.

Sample daily template
- Breakfast: Oats with berries, walnuts, chia/flax; or veggie omelet + whole-grain toast; or Greek yogurt parfait.
- Lunch: Lentil/bean soup + salad; quinoa bowl with chickpeas/veg/EVOO; or whole-grain wrap (grilled chicken/tempeh + hummus + veg).
- Dinner: Salmon + farro + broccoli; chicken + sweet potato + greens; or bean chili over brown rice + salad.
- Snacks: Fruit + nuts; carrots + hummus; plain yogurt with berries; cottage cheese + pineapple; edamame; popcorn (unsalted).

Recovery and adjuncts
- Sleep: 7–8 hours, consistent schedule.
- Creatine monohydrate: Discuss with cardiologist; if approved and renal function normal, 3 g/day (no loading) may aid strength.
- Avoid NSAIDs for soreness unless advised; use mobility, light walking, or 10–15 min easy cycling to reduce DOMS.

Substitutions for joint comfort
- Knees: Use leg press or hack squat (shallow) instead of squats; low box step-ups/TRX-assisted squat.
- Low back/hips: Glute bridge/hip thrust or cable pull-through instead of deadlifts.
- Shoulders/wrists: Smith box squat or safety-bar squat; swap cable press angles as needed.

Monitoring
- Keep a simple log: exercises, sets/reps, loads, peak HR, RPE, symptoms. Record cardio minutes and steps.
- If HR or RPE regularly exceed targets, reduce next session volume by 10–20% or add rest day.
- Coordinate with his cardiologist/dietitian for medication–nutrition interactions and any update to exercise clearance (especially before any performance testing or intensity changes).

This integrated plan builds practical strength with safe compound patterns, meaningfully increases weekly cardio for weight loss within moderate limits, and aligns nutrition to cardiac health and recovery over the full 12 weeks.
